angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 527,341 km at 42.01 pc = 0.17 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 23.8052 +/- 0.0125 mas (same row, RUWE 0.98): 42.01 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.758 +/- 0.03 solar radii from Wang et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2076 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026NatAs..10..818W/abstract): 527,341 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.849 +/- 0.026 solar masses from Wang et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2076 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026NatAs..10..818W/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5192 +/- 61 K from Barber et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of TOI-2076 e's parameter set from Barber et al. 2025 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170...32B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Barber et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of TOI-2076 e's parameter set from Barber et al. 2025 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170...32B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2076.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.608, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
